profile_md: MIT's employer-linked group project provision is concentrated in graduate professional programmes, with no institute-wide scheme verified. The clearest route is MIT Sloan Action Learning: four-person teams with a faculty mentor tackle a host organisation's real problem and deliver options and recommendations; hosts name an executive sponsor and contact and fund travel, and Sloan reports work with over 2,700 organisations. Further Sloan routes are the MBA-core OP Team Project (teams of six, live company case, all first-year MBAs) and the Master of Business Analytics capstone (38 external sponsors in 2025, mostly student pairs, sponsors provide a staff mentor and data). Engineering-side master's routes are the Supply Chain Management capstone (10-month sponsor-defined projects) and the SDM spring project (industry, government and non-profit partners), and D-Lab and DUSP offer partner/client semester projects. Undergraduate options are thin: NEET is team- and project-based with industry sponsorship but no employer-set group project was evidenced, and UROP is individual research. Most records rest on undated pages, so current delivery is confirmed only for Action Learning (Work Lab, spring 2026) and the MBAn capstone (2027 call). Access is programme-specific, mostly postgraduate taught.
gaps: Session limit stopped further fetches: SCM page not opened by WebFetch (summary only); undergraduate departmental capstones (1.013, 16.82, 6.UAP etc.), Gordon Engineering Leadership, UPOP, MISTI, Media Lab and Architecture not researched; science area had only one query; further departmental instances likely. Credit, compulsory status and dated delivery missing for S2-S7. WebFetch summaries (small model) rather than verbatim quotes.
